The program uses a regular expression to find every assignment of the form `name <- expression;` in the input. It supports the two expression shapes that appear in the text: a plain integer, or `(var + N) mod 100`. Any other expression stops the program with an error rather than being skipped. It then prints the final values in the requested order.

```python
import sys
import re

def main():
    text = sys.stdin.read()
    env = {}
    stmt_re = re.compile(r'([A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*<-\s*([^;]+);')
    num_re = re.compile(r'^\s*(-?\d+)\s*$')
    add_re = re.compile(r'^\s*\(\s*([A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*([+\-])\s*(-?\d+)\s*\)\s*mod\s*(\d+)\s*$')
    for m in stmt_re.finditer(text):
        name, expr = m.group(1), m.group(2)
        mm = num_re.match(expr)
        if mm:
            env[name] = int(mm.group(1))
            continue
        mm = add_re.match(expr)
        if mm:
            var, op, n, mod = mm.group(1), mm.group(2), int(mm.group(3)), int(mm.group(4))
            cur = env.get(var, 0)
            val = cur + n if op == '+' else cur - n
            env[name] = val % mod
            continue
        raise SystemExit("Unrecognized expression: %r" % (m.group(0),))
    order = list("abcdefghijklmnop") + ["TMP"]
    print(" ".join("%s ?= %d;" % (v, env.get(v, 0)) for v in order))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```
